actions-list.actionItem: Pursuant to the order of yesterday, the Journal of the proceedings of the Senate was deemed approved to date.
Pursuant to the order of yesterday,the morning hour being deemed expired, and the times for the recognition of the two leaders being reserved.
The following transactions of morning business occurred on today.

H.R. 2388 (Rep. Randall):
        A bill to take certain Federal land in the State of Washington into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.Con.Res. 89 (Rep. Jayapal):
        A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

        -- Senate Committee on Foreign Relations discharged, under the order of 8/8/26

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Failed of passage in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 49 - 50. Record Vote Number: 244 



 S. 240 (Sen. Daines):
        A bill to amend the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 to make improvements to that Act, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate agreed to the House amendment to S. 240 by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 283 (Sen. Cruz):
        A bill to require the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and the Administrator of National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement againstillegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate agreed to the House amendment to S. 283 by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 3257 (Sen. Hoeven):
        A bill to require the Administrator of the FederalAviation Administration to revise regulations for certain individuals carrying out aviation activities who disclose a mental health diagnosis or condition, and for other purposes.

        -- The committee substitute withdrawn by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 6834 (Sen. Hoeven):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 6834 proposed by Senator Husted for Senator Hoeven.

        --Amendment SA 6834 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 3258 (Sen. Duckworth):
        A bill to require the Administrator of the FederalAviation Administration to publish the list of medications that the Administrator has compiled for purposes of the medical certification of airmen and air traffic control specialists, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 4668 (Sen. Cruz):
        A bill to protect the name, image, and likeness rights of, and provide protections for, student athletes and to promote fair competition among intercollegiate athletics, and for other purposes.

        -- Considered by Senate.

        -- Cloture on the measure, as amended, invoked in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 74 -25. Record Vote Number: 243 


        -- The committee substitute withdrawn by Voice Vote.
 

 S.Amdt. 6776 (Sen. Cruz):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Considered by Senate.

        --Amendment SA 6776 agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 77 - 23. Record Vote Number: 


 S.Amdt. 6777 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.

        --Motion to table amendment SA 6777 agreed to in Senate by Voice Vote.


 S.Amdt. 6778 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.

        --SA 6778 fell when SA 6777 was tabled.


 S.Amdt. 6779 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.

        --Motion to table amendment SA 6779 agreed to in Senate by Voice Vote.


 S.Amdt. 6780 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.

        --SA 6780 fell when SA 6779 was tabled.




 S.Res. 902 (Sen. Schatz):
        A resolution supporting the designation of the week of September 20 through September 26, 2026, as "Telehealth Awareness Week".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 903 (Sen. Blackburn):
        A resolution designating October 30, 2026, as a national day of remembrance for the workers of the nuclear weapons program of the United States.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 904 (Sen. Hyde-Smith):
        A resolution designating the week of September 20 through September 27, 2026, as "Gold Star Families Remembrance Week".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 905 (Sen. King):
        A resolution designating September 25, 2026, as "National Lobster Day".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.
By unanimous consent, on the request of Mr. Husted, at  4:05 p.m., the Senate adjourned, under its order of today, until  3 p.m. on Monday, September 28, 2026.
